1	# Introduction to Dispatch
2	
3	CLI applications typically mix business logic with output formatting: database queries interleaved with `println!`, validation tangled with ANSI codes, error handling scattered across presentation. The result is code that's hard to test, hard to change, and impossible to reuse.
4	
5	`standout-dispatch` enforces a clean separation:
6	
7	```text
8	CLI args → Handler (adapter) → View data → consuming framework
9	```
10	
11	- **Handlers** receive parsed arguments, return serializable data
12	- **Hooks** intercept execution at defined points
13	
14	This isn't just architectural nicety—it unlocks:
15	
16	- **Testable handlers** — Typed adapters with explicit inputs and outputs
17	- **Reusable results** — JSON, templates, and plain text can all start from the same handler data
18	- **Cross-cutting concerns** — Auth, logging, transformation via hooks
19	- **Incremental adoption** — Migrate one command at a time
20	
21	---
22	
23	## The Problem
24	
25	Here's a typical CLI command implementation:
26	
27	```rust
28	fn list_command(matches: &ArgMatches) {
29	    let verbose = matches.get_flag("verbose");
30	    let items = storage::list().expect("failed to list");
31	
32	    println!("\x1b[1;36mItems\x1b[0m");
33	    println!("──────");
34	    for item in &items {
35	        if verbose {
36	            println!("{}: {} (created: {})", item.id, item.name, item.created);
37	        } else {
38	            println!("{}: {}", item.id, item.name);
39	        }
40	    }
41	    println!("\n{} items total", items.len());
42	}
43	```
44	
45	Problems with this approach:
46	
47	1. **Testing is painful** — You have to capture stdout and parse it
48	2. **No format flexibility** — Want JSON output? Write a whole new function
49	3. **Error handling is crude** — `expect` or scattered error messages
50	4. **Logic and presentation intertwined** — Can't reuse the logic elsewhere
51	5. **Cross-cutting concerns require duplication** — Auth checks in every command
52	
53	---
54	
55	## The Solution: Handlers Return Data
56	
57	With `standout-dispatch`, handlers adapt CLI input into application calls and
58	return view data:
59	
60	```rust
61	use standout_dispatch::{Handler, Output, CommandContext, HandlerResult};
62	use serde::Serialize;
63	
64	#[derive(Serialize)]
65	struct ListResult {
66	    items: Vec<Item>,
67	    total: usize,
68	}
69	
70	fn list_handler(matches: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<ListResult> {
71	    let items = storage::list()?;  // Errors propagate naturally
72	    Ok(Output::Render(ListResult {
73	        total: items.len(),
74	        items,
75	    }))
76	}
77	```
78	
79	The handler:
80	
81	- Receives parsed arguments (`&ArgMatches`) and execution context
82	- Returns a `Result` with serializable data
83	- Contains zero presentation logic
84	
85	Presentation is handled separately by the caller or by the `standout` framework.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## Quick Start
90	
91	```toml
92	[dependencies]
93	standout-dispatch = "2.1"
94	clap = { version = "4", features = ["derive"] }
95	serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
96	serde_json = "1"
97	anyhow = "1"
98	```
99	
100	```rust
101	use standout_dispatch::{
102	    FnHandler, Output, CommandContext, HandlerResult,
103	    extract_command_path, path_to_string,
104	};
105	use clap::{Command, Arg};
106	use serde::Serialize;
107	
108	#[derive(Serialize)]
109	struct Greeting { message: String }
110	
111	fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
112	    // 1. Define clap command
113	    let cmd = Command::new("myapp")
114	        .subcommand(
115	            Command::new("greet")
116	                .arg(Arg::new("name").required(true))
117	        );
118	
119	    // 2. Create handler
120	    let greet_handler = FnHandler::new(|matches, _ctx| {
121	        let name: &String = matches.get_one("name").unwrap();
122	        Ok(Output::Render(Greeting {
123	            message: format!("Hello, {}!", name),
124	        }))
125	    });
126	
127	    // 3. Parse and dispatch
128	    let matches = cmd.get_matches();
129	    let path = extract_command_path(&matches);
130	
131	    if path_to_string(&path) == "greet" {
132	        let ctx = CommandContext { command_path: path };
133	        let result = greet_handler.handle(&matches, &ctx)?;
134	
135	        if let Output::Render(data) = result {
136	            println!("{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&data)?);
137	        }
138	    }
139	
140	    Ok(())
141	}
142	```
143	
144	---
145	
146	## The Output Enum
147	
148	Handlers return one of three output types:
149	
150	```rust
151	pub enum Output<T: Serialize> {
152	    Render(T),          // Data for rendering
153	    Silent,             // No output (side-effect commands)
154	    Binary {            // Raw bytes (file exports)
155	        data: Vec<u8>,
156	        filename: String,
157	    },
158	}
159	```
160	
161	### Output::Render(T)
162	
163	The common case. Data is passed to your render function:
164	
165	```rust
166	fn list_handler(_m: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<Vec<Item>> {
167	    let items = storage::list()?;
168	    Ok(Output::Render(items))
169	}
170	```
171	
172	### Output::Silent
173	
174	For commands with side effects only:
175	
176	```rust
177	fn delete_handler(matches: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<()> {
178	    let id: &String = matches.get_one("id").unwrap();
179	    storage::delete(id)?;
180	    Ok(Output::Silent)
181	}
182	```
183	
184	### Output::Binary
185	
186	For generating files:
187	
188	```rust
189	fn export_handler(_m: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<()> {
190	    let data = generate_report()?;
191	    let csv_bytes = format_as_csv(&data)?;
192	
193	    Ok(Output::Binary {
194	        data: csv_bytes.into_bytes(),
195	        filename: "report.csv".into(),
196	    })
197	}
198	```
199	
200	---
201	
202	## State Management
203	
204	Handlers access state through `CommandContext`, which provides two injection mechanisms:
205	
206	### App State (Shared)
207	
208	Configure long-lived resources at build time:
209	
210	```rust
211	use standout::cli::App;
212	
213	struct Database { /* connection pool */ }
214	struct Config { api_url: String }
215	
216	App::builder()
217	    .app_state(Database::connect()?)  // Shared across all dispatches
218	    .app_state(Config::load()?)
219	    .command("list", list_handler, "{{ items }}")
220	    .build()?
221	```
222	
223	Access in handlers via `ctx.app_state`:
224	
225	```rust
226	fn list_handler(matches: &ArgMatches, ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<Vec<Item>> {
227	    let db = ctx.app_state.get_required::<Database>()?;
228	    let config = ctx.app_state.get_required::<Config>()?;
229	    Ok(Output::Render(db.list(&config.api_url)?))
230	}
231	```
232	
233	### Extensions (Per-Request)
234	
235	Pre-dispatch hooks inject request-scoped state via `ctx.extensions`:
236	
237	```rust
238	Hooks::new().pre_dispatch(|matches, ctx| {
239	    let user_id = matches.get_one::<String>("user").unwrap();
240	    ctx.extensions.insert(UserScope { user_id: user_id.clone() });
241	    Ok(())
242	})
243	```
244	
245	> For full details, see [App State and Extensions](../topics/app-state.md).
246	
247	---
248	
249	## Hooks: Cross-Cutting Concerns
250	
251	Hooks let you intercept execution without modifying handler logic:
252	
253	```rust
254	use standout_dispatch::{Hooks, HookError, RenderedOutput};
255	
256	let hooks = Hooks::new()
257	    // Before handler: validation, auth, inject per-request state
258	    .pre_dispatch(|matches, ctx| {
259	        if !is_authenticated() {
260	            return Err(HookError::pre_dispatch("auth required"));
261	        }
262	        Ok(())
263	    })
264	    // After handler, before render: transform data
265	    .post_dispatch(|_m, _ctx, mut data| {
266	        if let Some(obj) = data.as_object_mut() {
267	            obj.insert("timestamp".into(), json!(Utc::now().to_rfc3339()));
268	        }
269	        Ok(data)
270	    })
271	    // After render: transform output
272	    .post_output(|_m, _ctx, output| {
273	        if let RenderedOutput::Text(s) = output {
274	            Ok(RenderedOutput::Text(format!("{}\n-- footer", s)))
275	        } else {
276	            Ok(output)
277	        }
278	    });
279	```
280	
281	### Hook Phases
282	
283	| Phase | Timing | Receives | Can |
284	| ------- | -------- | ---------- | ----- |
285	| `pre_dispatch` | Before handler | ArgMatches, **&mut** Context | Abort execution, inject state |
286	| `post_dispatch` | After handler, before render | ArgMatches, Context, Data | Transform data |
287	| `post_output` | After render | ArgMatches, Context, Output | Transform output |
288	
289	> **State Injection:** Pre-dispatch hooks can inject dependencies via `ctx.extensions` that handlers retrieve. This enables dependency injection without changing handler signatures. See [Handler Contract: Extensions](../topics/handler-contract.md#extensions) for details.
290	
291	### Hook Chaining
292	
293	Multiple hooks per phase run sequentially:
294	
295	```rust
296	Hooks::new()
297	    .post_dispatch(add_metadata)      // Runs first
298	    .post_dispatch(filter_sensitive)  // Receives add_metadata's output
299	```
300	
301	---
302	
303	## Handler Types
304	
305	### Closure Handlers
306	
307	Most handlers are simple closures:
308	
309	```rust
310	let handler = FnHandler::new(|matches, ctx| {
311	    let name: &String = matches.get_one("name").unwrap();
312	    Ok(Output::Render(Data { name: name.clone() }))
313	});
314	```
315	
316	### Trait Implementations
317	
318	For handlers with internal state:
319	
320	```rust
321	struct DbHandler {
322	    pool: DatabasePool,
323	}
324	
325	impl Handler for DbHandler {
326	    type Output = Vec<Row>;
327	
328	    fn handle(&self, matches: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<Vec<Row>> {
329	        let query: &String = matches.get_one("query").unwrap();
330	        let rows = self.pool.query(query)?;
331	        Ok(Output::Render(rows))
332	    }
333	}
334	```
335	
336	### Struct Handlers (With State)
337	
338	When handlers need internal state with `&mut self`:
339	
340	```rust
341	impl Handler for Cache {
342	    type Output = Data;
343	
344	    fn handle(&mut self, matches: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<Data> {
345	        self.invalidate();  // &mut self works
346	        Ok(Output::Render(self.get()?))
347	    }
348	}
349	```
350	
351	See [Handler Contract](../topics/handler-contract.md) for full details.
352	
353	---
354	
355	## Command Routing Utilities
356	
357	Extract and navigate clap's `ArgMatches`:
358	
359	```rust
360	use standout_dispatch::{
361	    extract_command_path,
362	    get_deepest_matches,
363	    has_subcommand,
364	    path_to_string,
365	};
366	
367	// myapp db migrate --steps 5
368	let path = extract_command_path(&matches);  // ["db", "migrate"]
369	let path_str = path_to_string(&path);       // "db.migrate"
370	let deep = get_deepest_matches(&matches);   // ArgMatches for "migrate"
371	```
372	
373	---
374	
375	## Testing Handlers
376	
377	Because handlers have explicit inputs and outputs, testing their CLI adapter
378	behavior is straightforward:
379	
380	```rust
381	#[test]
382	fn test_list_handler() {
383	    let cmd = Command::new("test")
384	        .arg(Arg::new("verbose").long("verbose").action(ArgAction::SetTrue));
385	    let matches = cmd.try_get_matches_from(["test", "--verbose"]).unwrap();
386	
387	    let ctx = CommandContext {
388	        command_path: vec!["list".into()],
389	    };
390	
391	    let result = list_handler(&matches, &ctx);
392	
393	    assert!(result.is_ok());
394	    if let Ok(Output::Render(data)) = result {
395	        assert!(data.verbose);
396	    }
397	}
398	```
399	
400	No mocking needed—construct `ArgMatches` with clap, call your handler, assert on the result.
401	
402	---
403	
404	## Summary
405	
406	`standout-dispatch` provides:
407	
408	1. **Clean separation** — Handlers return data, renderers produce output
409	2. **Pluggable rendering** — Use any output format without changing handlers
410	3. **Hook system** — Cross-cutting concerns without code duplication
411	4. **Testable design** — CLI-free library behavior and typed handler adapters have explicit contracts
412	5. **Incremental adoption** — Migrate one command at a time
413	
414	For complete API details, see the [API documentation](https://docs.rs/standout-dispatch).
415	
416	> **For standout framework users:** The framework provides full integration with templates and themes. See the standout documentation for the `App` and `AppBuilder` APIs that wire dispatch and render together automatically.

1	# App Configuration
2	
3	`AppBuilder` is the unified entry point for configuring your application. Instead of scattering configuration across multiple structs (`Standout`, `RenderSetup`, `Theme`), everything from command registration to theme selection happens in one fluent interface.
4	
5	This design ensures that your application defines its entire environment—commands, styles, templates, and hooks—before the runtime starts, preventing configuration race conditions and simplifying testing.
6	
7	This guide covers the full setup: embedding resources, registering commands, configuring themes, and customizing behavior.
8	
9	See also:
10	
11	- [Rendering System](rendering-system.md) for details on templates and styles.
12	- [Topics System](topics-system.md) for help topics.
13	
14	## Basic Setup
15	
16	```rust
17	use standout::cli::App;
18	use standout_macros::{embed_templates, embed_styles};
19	
20	let app = App::builder()
21	    .templates(embed_templates!("src/templates"))
22	    .styles(embed_styles!("src/styles"))
23	    .default_theme("default")
24	    .command_with("list", list_handler, |config| config.template_name("list"))?
25	    .build()?;
26	
27	app.run(Cli::command(), std::env::args());
28	```
29	
30	## Embedding Resources
31	
32	### Templates
33	
34	`embed_templates!` embeds template files at compile time:
35	
36	```rust
37	.templates(embed_templates!("src/templates"))
38	```
39	
40	Collects files matching: `.jinja`, `.jinja2`, `.j2`, `.stpl`, `.txt` (in priority order).
41	
42	> **Custom template engines:** For advanced use cases, `standout-render` supports pluggable template engines. See the [Template Engines](../crates/standout-render/docs/topics/template-engines.md) topic for details on using `SimpleEngine` or implementing custom engines.
43	
44	Directory structure:
45	
46	```text
47	src/templates/
48	  list.j2
49	  add.j2
50	  db/
51	    migrate.j2
52	    status.j2
53	```
54	
55	Templates are referenced by path without extension: `"list"`, `"db/migrate"`.
56	
57	### Styles
58	
59	`embed_styles!` embeds stylesheet files:
60	
61	```rust
62	.styles(embed_styles!("src/styles"))
63	```
64	
65	Collects files matching: `.css` (and legacy `.yaml`, `.yml`).
66	
67	```text
68	src/styles/
69	  default.css
70	  dark.css
71	  light.css
72	```
73	
74	Themes are referenced by filename without extension: `"default"`, `"dark"`.
75	
76	### Hot Reloading
77	
78	In debug builds, embedded resources are re-read from disk on each render—edit without recompiling. In release builds, embedded content is used directly.
79	
80	This is automatic when the source path exists on disk.
81	
82	## Runtime Overrides
83	
84	Users can override embedded resources with local files:
85	
86	```rust
87	App::builder()
88	    .templates(embed_templates!("src/templates"))
89	    .templates_dir("~/.myapp/templates")  // Overrides embedded
90	    .styles(embed_styles!("src/styles"))
91	    .styles_dir("~/.myapp/themes")        // Overrides embedded
92	```
93	
94	Local directories take precedence. This enables user customization without recompiling.
95	
96	## Theme Selection
97	
98	### From Stylesheet Registry
99	
100	```rust
101	    .styles(embed_styles!("src/styles"))
102	    // Optional: set explicit default name
103	    // If omitted, tries "default", "theme", then "base"
104	    .default_theme("dark")
105	```
106	
107	If `.default_theme()` is not called, `AppBuilder` attempts to load a theme from the registry in this order:
108	
109	1. `default`
110	2. `theme`
111	3. `base`
112	
113	This allows you to provide a standard `base.css` or `theme.css` without requiring explicit configuration code. If the explicit theme isn't found, `build()` returns `SetupError::ThemeNotFound`.
114	
115	### Explicit Theme
116	
117	```rust
118	let theme = Theme::new()
119	    .add("title", Style::new().bold().cyan())
120	    .add("muted", Style::new().dim());
121	
122	App::builder()
123	    .theme(theme)  // Overrides stylesheet registry
124	```
125	
126	Explicit `.theme()` takes precedence over `.default_theme()`.
127	
128	## Command Registration
129	
130	### Simple Commands
131	
132	```rust
133	App::builder()
134	    .command("list", list_handler, "[title]Items[/title]")
135	    .command("add", add_handler, "Added {{ name }}")
136	```
137	
138	Arguments: command name, handler function, inline MiniJinja template source.
139	
140	### With Configuration
141	
142	```rust
143	App::builder()
144	    .command_with("delete", delete_handler, |cfg| cfg
145	        .template_name("delete")
146	        .pre_dispatch(require_confirmation)
147	        .post_dispatch(log_deletion))
148	```
149	
150	Inline command configuration can also attach a
151	`StructuredOutputProjection` for CSV shaping. The projection stays at the
152	presentation boundary: it sees post-dispatch data, and handlers remain
153	independent of the selected output mode. See [Output Modes](output-modes.md#csv-output).
154	
155	### Nested Groups
156	
157	```rust
158	App::builder()
159	    .group("db", |g| g
160	        .command("migrate", migrate_handler, "Migrated")
161	        .command("status", status_handler, "Status: {{ status }}")
162	        .group("backup", |b| b
163	            .command("create", backup_create, "Backup created")
164	            .command("restore", backup_restore, "Backup restored")))
165	```
166	
167	Creates command paths: `db.migrate`, `db.status`, `db.backup.create`, `db.backup.restore`.
168	
169	### From Dispatch Macro
170	
171	```rust
172	#[derive(Dispatch)]
173	enum Commands {
174	    List,
175	    Add,
176	    #[dispatch(nested)]
177	    Db(DbCommands),
178	}
179	
180	App::builder()
181	    .commands(Commands::dispatch_config())?
182	```
183	
184	The macro generates registration for all variants.
185	
186	## Default Command
187	
188	When a CLI is invoked without a subcommand (a "naked" invocation like `myapp` or `myapp --verbose`), you can specify a default command to run:
189	
190	```rust
191	App::builder()
192	    .default_command("list")
193	    .command("list", list_handler, "{{ items | length }} items")
194	    .command("add", add_handler, "Added {{ name }}")
195	```
196	
197	With this configuration:
198	
199	- `myapp` becomes `myapp list`
200	- `myapp --output=json` becomes `myapp list --output=json`
201	- `myapp add foo` stays as `myapp add foo` (explicit command takes precedence)
202	
203	Default resolution applies to both the integrated dispatch path (`run`, `dispatch_from`, `run_to_string`) and configured parsing (`parse_from`, `get_matches_from`). If you parse first and build dispatch state afterwards, the matches you get back already name the resolved command.
204	
205	### Invocation-Aware Defaults
206	
207	A fixed name can't express "it depends". `default_command_with` chooses the default per invocation:
208	
209	```rust
210	App::builder()
211	    .default_command_with(|ctx| {
212	        Some(if ctx.stdin_is_piped() { "add" } else { "list" }.to_string())
213	    })
214	    .command("list", list_handler, "{{ items | length }} items")
215	    .command("add", add_handler, "Added {{ name }}")
216	```
217	
218	- `myapp` at a terminal becomes `myapp list`
219	- `cat notes.txt | myapp` becomes `myapp add`, which reads the pipe
220	- `myapp done 3` stays as `myapp done 3`
221	
222	The resolver receives a `DefaultCommandContext` exposing only the facts needed to pick a command:
223	
224	| Method | Fact |
225	| --- | --- |
226	| `matches()` | The parsed root `ArgMatches` — globals and root flags |
227	| `app_state::<T>()` | Read-only app state registered via `.app_state(...)` |
228	| `stdin_is_terminal()` / `stdin_is_piped()` | Whether stdin is redirected |
229	
230	Plus `std::env` for env-derived facts. The matches are the root's, so global flags and root arguments are all there; there is no subcommand, because that is what makes the invocation naked.
231	
232	**Stdin is never read during resolution.** The terminal check is the same non-consuming `StdinReader::is_terminal` seam the input system uses, so a handler's `InputChain` still consumes the pipe normally afterwards. This also means piped-but-empty stdin is a *pipe*, not a terminal — emptiness is only knowable by reading, which resolution never does. If empty input should be an error, that's the receiving command's `InputChain` policy, not the resolver's.
233	
234	### Ordering guarantees
235	
236	**Clap decides which command a line named**, and resolution reads that decision. A parse that selected a subcommand is not naked; a parse that selected none is.
237	
238	- **Explicit and nested commands** short-circuit resolution — the resolver never runs.
239	- **`--help` / `--version`** are Clap's own displays: no default is inserted, so `myapp --help` renders the root's help rather than a default command's.
240	- **Invalid syntax** stays a Clap usage error (exit 2). If a default command is configured, a refused line is offered to it — `myapp --all` is a naked line at a root that has no `--all`, and becomes `myapp list --all` when `--all` belongs to `list` — and whatever the amended line parses to, success or failure, is what you get.
241	- **`--`**, option values, aliases, and short clusters mean exactly what they mean everywhere else, because the same parser reads them.
242	
243	A root that requires a subcommand — what `#[command(subcommand)] command: Commands` produces — still accepts a naked invocation: the line is refused, the default is substituted, and the amended line parses. The field does not have to be `Option<Commands>`. See [ADR-0018](../adr/0018-let-the-parser-classify-the-command-line.md).
244	
245	### Combining both
246	
247	Both may be configured together. The resolver is consulted first; returning `None` declines to the static default:
248	
249	```rust
250	App::builder()
251	    // Pipes mean `add`; everything else falls back to `list`.
252	    .default_command("list")
253	    .default_command_with(|ctx| ctx.stdin_is_piped().then(|| "add".to_string()))
254	```
255	
256	Returning a name that isn't a command of your `clap::Command` fails the run with `RunErrorKind::DefaultCommand` (exit 1), carrying a diagnostic that names the offending resolver output and lists the valid commands. A resolver naming a command the CLI doesn't have is an application bug, so it's reported as one rather than reaching Clap as a usage error blaming the user. Return `None` to decline.
257	
258	Validation is against your `clap::Command`'s names, not Standout's registered handlers — so partial adoption stays coherent: resolving to a Clap command Standout doesn't handle yields `NoMatch`, exactly as typing it explicitly would.
259	
260	### With Dispatch Macro
261	
262	Use the `#[dispatch(default)]` attribute to mark a variant as the default:
263	
264	```rust
265	#[derive(Dispatch)]
266	#[dispatch(handlers = handlers)]
267	enum Commands {
268	    #[dispatch(default)]
269	    List,
270	    Add,
271	}
272	
273	App::builder()
274	    .commands(Commands::dispatch_config())?
275	```
276	
277	Only one command can be marked as default. Multiple `#[dispatch(default)]` attributes will cause a compile error.
278	
279	## Hooks
280	
281	Attach hooks to specific command paths:
282	
283	```rust
284	App::builder()
285	    .command("migrate", migrate_handler, "Migrated")
286	    .hooks("db.migrate", Hooks::new()
287	        .pre_dispatch(require_admin)
288	        .post_dispatch(add_timestamp)
289	        .post_output(log_result))
290	```
291	
292	The path uses dot notation matching the command hierarchy.
293	
294	## Context Injection
295	
296	Add values available in all templates:
297	
298	### Static Context
299	
300	```rust
301	App::builder()
302	    .context("version", "1.0.0")
303	    .context("app_name", "MyApp")
304	```
305	
306	### Dynamic Context
307	
308	```rust
309	App::builder()
310	    .context_fn("terminal_width", |ctx| {
311	        Value::from(ctx.terminal_width.unwrap_or(80))
312	    })
313	    .context_fn("timestamp", |_ctx| {
314	        Value::from(chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339())
315	    })
316	```
317	
318	Dynamic providers receive `RenderContext` with output mode, terminal width, and handler data.
319	They also receive `ctx.ambiguous_width()`, the application's explicit
320	East Asian Ambiguous character-width policy. Configure it at the rendering
321	seam; narrow is the compatibility default and Standout does not infer a locale:
322	
323	```rust
324	use standout::{AmbiguousWidth, cli::App};
325	
326	let app = App::builder()
327	    .ambiguous_width(AmbiguousWidth::Wide)
328	    .build()?;
329	```
330	
331	## Topics
332	
333	Add help topics:
334	
335	```rust
336	App::builder()
337	    .topics_dir("docs/topics")
338	    .add_topic(Topic::new("auth", "Authentication...", TopicType::Text, None))
339	```
340	
341	See [Topics System](topics-system.md) for details.
342	
343	## Version
344	
345	Application version metadata belongs on the builder, next to the rest of the
346	app's configuration:
347	
348	```rust
349	App::builder()
350	    .version(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"))
351	```
352	
353	Standout applies the value to the root command wherever it augments and parses
354	it, so every entry point — `run`, `run_to_string`, `dispatch_from`,
355	`get_matches_from`, and `TestHarness` — answers `myapp --version` the same way:
356	Clap's own display, on stdout, exit status 0, typed as
357	`SuccessKind::ClapVersion` (see [Execution
358	Outcomes](./execution-outcomes.md)).
359	
360	Clap keeps owning the spelling and formatting of that output and the display
361	short-circuit; the builder only says what the version is. Leave `.version()`
362	unset and the supplied `clap::Command` is untouched, including a version
363	configured on Clap directly.
364	
365	This is separate from `.context("version", …)`, which puts a value in *templates*
366	(`{{ version }}`); an app that wants both says both.
367	
368	## Flag Customization
369	
370	### Output Flag
371	
372	```rust
373	App::builder()
374	    .output_flag(Some("format"))  // --format instead of --output
375	```
376	
377	```rust
378	App::builder()
379	    .no_output_flag()  // Disable entirely
380	```
381	
382	### File Output Flag
383	
384	```rust
385	App::builder()
386	    .output_file_flag(Some("out"))  // --out instead of --output-file-path
387	```
388	
389	```rust
390	App::builder()
391	    .no_output_file_flag()  // Disable entirely
392	```
393	
394	## The App Struct
395	
396	`build()` produces an `App`:
397	
398	```rust
399	pub struct App {
400	    registry: TopicRegistry,
401	    output_flag: Option<String>,
402	    output_file_flag: Option<String>,
403	    output_mode: OutputMode,
404	    theme: Option<Theme>,
405	    command_hooks: HashMap<String, Hooks>,
406	    template_registry: Option<TemplateRegistry>,
407	    stylesheet_registry: Option<StylesheetRegistry>,
408	}
409	```
410	
411	## Running the App
412	
413	### Standard Execution
414	
415	```rust
416	if !app.run(Cli::command(), std::env::args()) {
417	    // Standout did not handle this command; fall back to legacy dispatch.
418	    legacy_dispatch();
419	}
420	```
421	
422	Parses args, dispatches to a handler, and performs the final write. It returns
423	`true` when Standout handled the command and `false` for an unmatched fallback.
424	Help/version and successes use stdout/status 0, usage errors use stderr/status
425	2, and runtime/write failures use stderr/status 1. An explicit
426	`ExternalFailure` is the sole exception: it preserves an authoritative external
427	operation's declared nonzero status and verbatim stderr payload.
428	
429	### Capture Output
430	
431	For testing, post-processing, or when you need the output string:
432	
433	```rust
434	match app.run_to_string(cmd, args) {
435	    RunResult::Handled(output) => { /* use output string */ }
436	    RunResult::Binary(bytes, filename) => { /* handle binary */ }
437	    RunResult::Error(error) => { /* inspect error.kind() */ }
438	    RunResult::NoMatch(matches) => { /* fallback dispatch */ }
439	    _ => {}
440	}
441	```
442	
443	Returns `RunResult` instead of printing. Use `exit_status()`, `success_kind()`,
444	and `error_kind()` for typed assertions; see [Execution
445	Outcomes](./execution-outcomes.md).
446	
447	### Parse Only
448	
449	```rust
450	let matches = app.parse_with(cmd);
451	// Use matches for manual dispatch
452	```
453	
454	Parses with Standout's augmented command but doesn't dispatch.
455	
456	## Build Validation
457	
458	`build()` validates:
459	
460	- a theme registry exists and contains the theme named by `.default_theme(...)`
461	- named templates resolve through `.templates(...)` or `.templates_dir(...)`
462	- convention templates resolve when application templates are configured; without application templates, human-mode rendering reports the missing convention template at runtime
463	- registered templates compile
464	- framework templates only use tags defined by the resolved theme
465	- `command_groups`, topics, and `help_word(true)` are paired with `.help_handling(true)`
466	- commands do not collide with the `help` word installed by `.help_handling(true)`
467	- the same command path and hook phase are not configured through both `CommandConfig` and `AppBuilder::hooks`
468	
469	What's NOT validated at build time:
470	
471	- Command handlers
472	- Hook signatures (verified at registration)
473	
474	## Complete Example
475	
476	```rust
477	use standout::cli::{App, CommandContext, HandlerResult, Output};
478	use standout_macros::{embed_templates, embed_styles};
479	use clap::{Command, ArgMatches};
480	use serde::Serialize;
481	
482	#[derive(Serialize)]
483	struct ListOutput {
484	    items: Vec<String>,
485	}
486	
487	fn list_handler(matches: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<ListOutput> {
488	    let items = vec!["one".into(), "two".into()];
489	    Ok(Output::Render(ListOutput { items }))
490	}
491	
492	fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
493	    let cli = Command::new("myapp")
494	        .subcommand(Command::new("list").about("List items"));
495	
496	    let app = App::builder()
497	        .templates(embed_templates!("src/templates"))
498	        .styles(embed_styles!("src/styles"))
499	        .default_theme("default")
500	        .version(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"))
501	        .context("version", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION").into())
502	        .command_with("list", list_handler, |config| {
503	            config.template_name("list")
504	        })?
505	        .topics_dir("docs/topics")?
506	        .help_handling(true)
507	        .build()?;
508	
509	    app.run(cli, std::env::args());
510	    Ok(())
511	}
512	```
513	
514	Template `src/templates/list.j2`:
515	
516	```jinja
517	[header]Items[/header] ({{ items | length }} total)
518	{% for item in items %}
519	  - {{ item }}
520	{% endfor %}
521	
522	[muted]v{{ version }}[/muted]
523	```
524	
525	Style `src/styles/default.css`:
526	
527	```css
528	.header { color: cyan; font-weight: bold; }
529	.muted { opacity: 0.5; }
530	```

# App Configuration

`AppBuilder` is the unified entry point for configuring your application. Instead of scattering configuration across multiple structs (`Standout`, `RenderSetup`, `Theme`), everything from command registration to theme selection happens in one fluent interface.

This design ensures that your application defines its entire environment—commands, styles, templates, and hooks—before the runtime starts, preventing configuration race conditions and simplifying testing.

This guide covers the full setup: embedding resources, registering commands, configuring themes, and customizing behavior.

See also:

- [Rendering System](rendering-system.md) for details on templates and styles.
- [Topics System](topics-system.md) for help topics.

## Basic Setup

```rust
use standout::cli::App;
use standout_macros::{embed_templates, embed_styles};

let app = App::builder()
    .templates(embed_templates!("src/templates"))
    .styles(embed_styles!("src/styles"))
    .default_theme("default")
    .command_with("list", list_handler, |config| config.template_name("list"))?
    .build()?;

app.run(Cli::command(), std::env::args());
```

## Embedding Resources

### Templates

`embed_templates!` embeds template files at compile time:

```rust
.templates(embed_templates!("src/templates"))
```

Collects files matching: `.jinja`, `.jinja2`, `.j2`, `.stpl`, `.txt` (in priority order).

> **Custom template engines:** For advanced use cases, `standout-render` supports pluggable template engines. See the [Template Engines](../crates/standout-render/docs/topics/template-engines.md) topic for details on using `SimpleEngine` or implementing custom engines.

Directory structure:

```text
src/templates/
  list.j2
  add.j2
  db/
    migrate.j2
    status.j2
```

Templates are referenced by path without extension: `"list"`, `"db/migrate"`.

### Styles

`embed_styles!` embeds stylesheet files:

```rust
.styles(embed_styles!("src/styles"))
```

Collects files matching: `.css` (and legacy `.yaml`, `.yml`).

```text
src/styles/
  default.css
  dark.css
  light.css
```

Themes are referenced by filename without extension: `"default"`, `"dark"`.

### Hot Reloading

In debug builds, embedded resources are re-read from disk on each render—edit without recompiling. In release builds, embedded content is used directly.

This is automatic when the source path exists on disk.

## Runtime Overrides

Users can override embedded resources with local files:

```rust
App::builder()
    .templates(embed_templates!("src/templates"))
    .templates_dir("~/.myapp/templates")  // Overrides embedded
    .styles(embed_styles!("src/styles"))
    .styles_dir("~/.myapp/themes")        // Overrides embedded
```

Local directories take precedence. This enables user customization without recompiling.

## Theme Selection

### From Stylesheet Registry

```rust
    .styles(embed_styles!("src/styles"))
    // Optional: set explicit default name
    // If omitted, tries "default", "theme", then "base"
    .default_theme("dark")
```

1. `default`
2. `theme`
3. `base`

### Explicit Theme

```rust
let theme = Theme::new()
    .add("title", Style::new().bold().cyan())
    .add("muted", Style::new().dim());

App::builder()
    .theme(theme)  // Overrides stylesheet registry
```

Explicit `.theme()` takes precedence over `.default_theme()`.

```rust
App::builder()
    .command("list", list_handler, "[title]Items[/title]")
    .command("add", add_handler, "Added {{ name }}")
```

```rust
App::builder()

        .post_dispatch(log_deletion))
```

`StructuredOutputProjection` for CSV shaping. The projection stays at the
presentation boundary: it sees post-dispatch data, and handlers remain
independent of the selected output mode. See [Output Modes](output-modes.md#csv-output).

### Nested Groups

```rust
App::builder()
    .group("db", |g| g
        .command("migrate", migrate_handler, "Migrated")
        .command("status", status_handler, "Status: {{ status }}")
        .group("backup", |b| b
            .command("create", backup_create, "Backup created")
            .command("restore", backup_restore, "Backup restored")))
```

Creates command paths: `db.migrate`, `db.status`, `db.backup.create`, `db.backup.restore`.

### From Dispatch Macro

```rust

enum Commands {
    List,
    Add,
    #[dispatch(nested)]

App::builder()
    .commands(Commands::dispatch_config())?
```

- **`--`**, option values, aliases, and short clusters mean exactly what they mean everywhere else, because the same parser reads them.

A root that requires a subcommand — what `#[command(subcommand)] command: Commands` produces — still accepts a naked invocation: the line is refused, the default is substituted, and the amended line parses. The field does not have to be `Option<Commands>`. See [ADR-0018](../adr/0018-let-the-parser-classify-the-command-line.md).

### Combining both

Both may be configured together. The resolver is consulted first; returning `None` declines to the static default:

```rust
App::builder()
    // Pipes mean `add`; everything else falls back to `list`.
    .default_command("list")
    .default_command_with(|ctx| ctx.stdin_is_piped().then(|| "add".to_string()))
```

Returning a name that isn't a command of your `clap::Command` fails the run with `RunErrorKind::DefaultCommand` (exit 1), carrying a diagnostic that names the offending resolver output and lists the valid commands. A resolver naming a command the CLI doesn't have is an application bug, so it's reported as one rather than reaching Clap as a usage error blaming the user. Return `None` to decline.

Validation is against your `clap::Command`'s names, not Standout's registered handlers — so partial adoption stays coherent: resolving to a Clap command Standout doesn't handle yields `NoMatch`, exactly as typing it explicitly would.

### With Dispatch Macro

Use the `#[dispatch(default)]` attribute to mark a variant as the default:

```rust
#[derive(Dispatch)]
#[dispatch(handlers = handlers)]
enum Commands {
    #[dispatch(default)]
    List,
    Add,
}

App::builder()
    .commands(Commands::dispatch_config())?
```

Only one command can be marked as default. Multiple `#[dispatch(default)]` attributes will cause a compile error.

## Hooks

Attach hooks to specific command paths:

```rust
App::builder()
    .command("migrate", migrate_handler, "Migrated")
    .hooks("db.migrate", Hooks::new()
        .pre_dispatch(require_admin)
        .post_dispatch(add_timestamp)
        .post_output(log_result))
```

The path uses dot notation matching the command hierarchy.

## Context Injection

Add values available in all templates:

### Static Context

```rust
App::builder()
    .context("version", "1.0.0")
    .context("app_name", "MyApp")
```

### Dynamic Context

```rust
App::builder()
    .context_fn("terminal_width", |ctx| {
        Value::from(ctx.terminal_width.unwrap_or(80))
    })
    .context_fn("timestamp", |_ctx| {
        Value::from(chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339())
    })
```

Dynamic providers receive `RenderContext` with output mode, terminal width, and handler data.
They also receive `ctx.ambiguous_width()`, the application's explicit
East Asian Ambiguous character-width policy. Configure it at the rendering
seam; narrow is the compatibility default and Standout does not infer a locale:

```rust
use standout::{AmbiguousWidth, cli::App};

let app = App::builder()
    .ambiguous_width(AmbiguousWidth::Wide)
    .build()?;
```

## Topics

Add help topics:

```rust
App::builder()
    .topics_dir("docs/topics")
    .add_topic(Topic::new("auth", "Authentication...", TopicType::Text, None))
```

See [Topics System](topics-system.md) for details.

## Version

Application version metadata belongs on the builder, next to the rest of the
app's configuration:

```rust
App::builder()
    .version(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"))
```

Standout applies the value to the root command wherever it augments and parses
it, so every entry point — `run`, `run_to_string`, `dispatch_from`,
`get_matches_from`, and `TestHarness` — answers `myapp --version` the same way:
Clap's own display, on stdout, exit status 0, typed as
`SuccessKind::ClapVersion` (see [Execution
Outcomes](./execution-outcomes.md)).

Clap keeps owning the spelling and formatting of that output and the display
short-circuit; the builder only says what the version is. Leave `.version()`
unset and the supplied `clap::Command` is untouched, including a version
configured on Clap directly.

This is separate from `.context("version", …)`, which puts a value in *templates*
(`{{ version }}`); an app that wants both says both.

## Flag Customization

### Output Flag

```rust
App::builder()
    .output_flag(Some("format"))  // --format instead of --output
```

```rust
App::builder()
    .no_output_flag()  // Disable entirely
```

### File Output Flag

```rust
App::builder()
    .output_file_flag(Some("out"))  // --out instead of --output-file-path
```

```rust
App::builder()
    .no_output_file_flag()  // Disable entirely
```

## The App Struct

`build()` produces an `App`:

```rust
pub struct App {
    registry: TopicRegistry,
    output_flag: Option<String>,
    output_file_flag: Option<String>,
    output_mode: OutputMode,
    theme: Option<Theme>,
    command_hooks: HashMap<String, Hooks>,
    template_registry: Option<TemplateRegistry>,
    stylesheet_registry: Option<StylesheetRegistry>,
}
```

## Running the App

### Standard Execution

```rust
if !app.run(Cli::command(), std::env::args()) {
    // Standout did not handle this command; fall back to legacy dispatch.
    legacy_dispatch();
}
```

Parses args, dispatches to a handler, and performs the final write. It returns
`true` when Standout handled the command and `false` for an unmatched fallback.
Help/version and successes use stdout/status 0, usage errors use stderr/status
2, and runtime/write failures use stderr/status 1. An explicit
`ExternalFailure` is the sole exception: it preserves an authoritative external
operation's declared nonzero status and verbatim stderr payload.

### Capture Output

For testing, post-processing, or when you need the output string:

```rust
match app.run_to_string(cmd, args) {
    RunResult::Handled(output) => { /* use output string */ }
    RunResult::Binary(bytes, filename) => { /* handle binary */ }
    RunResult::Error(error) => { /* inspect error.kind() */ }
    RunResult::NoMatch(matches) => { /* fallback dispatch */ }
    _ => {}
}
```

Returns `RunResult` instead of printing. Use `exit_status()`, `success_kind()`,
and `error_kind()` for typed assertions; see [Execution
Outcomes](./execution-outcomes.md).

### Parse Only

```rust
let matches = app.parse_with(cmd);
// Use matches for manual dispatch
```

Parses with Standout's augmented command but doesn't dispatch.

## Build Validation

`build()` validates:

- a theme registry exists and contains the theme named by `.default_theme(...)`
- named templates resolve through `.templates(...)` or `.templates_dir(...)`
- convention templates resolve when application templates are configured; without application templates, human-mode rendering reports the missing convention template at runtime
- registered templates compile
- framework templates only use tags defined by the resolved theme
- `command_groups`, topics, and `help_word(true)` are paired with `.help_handling(true)`
- commands do not collide with the `help` word installed by `.help_handling(true)`
- the same command path and hook phase are not configured through both `CommandConfig` and `AppBuilder::hooks`

What's NOT validated at build time:

- Command handlers
- Hook signatures (verified at registration)

## Complete Example

```rust
use standout::cli::{App, CommandContext, HandlerResult, Output};
use standout_macros::{embed_templates, embed_styles};
use clap::{Command, ArgMatches};
use serde::Serialize;

#[derive(Serialize)]
struct ListOutput {
    items: Vec<String>,
}

fn list_handler(matches: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<ListOutput> {
    let items = vec!["one".into(), "two".into()];
    Ok(Output::Render(ListOutput { items }))
}

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let cli = Command::new("myapp")
        .subcommand(Command::new("list").about("List items"));

    let app = App::builder()
        .templates(embed_templates!("src/templates"))
        .styles(embed_styles!("src/styles"))
        .default_theme("default")
        .version(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"))
        .context("version", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION").into())
        .command_with("list", list_handler, |config| {
            config.template_name("list")
        })?
        .topics_dir("docs/topics")?
        .help_handling(true)
        .build()?;

    app.run(cli, std::env::args());
    Ok(())
}
```

Template `src/templates/list.j2`:

```jinja
[header]Items[/header] ({{ items | length }} total)
{% for item in items %}
  - {{ item }}
{% endfor %}

[muted]v{{ version }}[/muted]
```

Style `src/styles/default.css`:

```css
.header { color: cyan; font-weight: bold; }
.muted { opacity: 0.5; }
```

content.content:
1	# The Handler Contract
2	
3	Handlers are shell adapters: they map parsed CLI input to application calls and
4	return serializable CLI-owned view data. Keep reusable behavior in a CLI-free
5	library. The handler contract is designed to be **explicit** rather than
6	permissive, so adapters remain testable and decoupled from output formatting.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## Quick Start: The `#[handler]` Macro
11	
12	For most handlers, use the `#[handler]` macro to write typed adapter functions:
13	
14	```rust
15	use standout_macros::handler;
16	
17	#[handler]
18	pub fn list(#[flag] all: bool, #[arg] limit: Option<usize>) -> Result<Vec<Item>, anyhow::Error> {
19	    storage::list(all, limit)
20	}
21	
22	// Generates: list__handler(&ArgMatches, &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<Vec<Item>>
23	```
24	
25	The macro:
26	
27	- Extracts CLI arguments from `ArgMatches` based on annotations
28	- Auto-wraps `Result<T, E>` in `Output::Render` via `IntoHandlerResult`
29	- Preserves the original function for direct testing
30	
31	**Parameter Annotations:**
32	
33	| Annotation            | Type              | Extraction                    |
34	| --------------------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------- |
35	| `#[flag]`             | `bool`            | `matches.get_flag("name")`    |
36	| `#[flag(name = "x")]` | `bool`            | `matches.get_flag("x")`       |
37	| `#[arg]`              | `T`               | Required argument             |
38	| `#[arg]`              | `Option<T>`       | Optional argument             |
39	| `#[arg]`              | `Vec<T>`          | Multiple values               |
40	| `#[arg(name = "x")]`  | `T`               | Argument with custom CLI name |
41	| `#[ctx]`              | `&CommandContext` | Access to context             |
42	| `#[matches]`          | `&ArgMatches`     | Raw matches (escape hatch)    |
43	
44	**Return Type Handling:**
45	
46	| Return Type     | Generated Wrapper                |
47	| --------------- | -------------------------------- |
48	| `Result<T, E>`  | Auto-wrapped in `Output::Render` |
49	| `Result<(), E>` | Wrapped in `Output::Silent`      |
50	
51	> **Testing:** The original function is preserved, so you can test directly: `list(true, Some(10))`.
52	
53	---
54	
55	## The Handler Trait
56	
57	```rust
58	pub trait Handler {
59	    type Output: Serialize;
60	    fn handle(&mut self, matches: &ArgMatches, ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<Self::Output>;
61	}
62	```
63	
64	Key characteristics:
65	
66	- **Mutable self**: `&mut self` allows direct state modification
67	- **Output must be Serialize**: Needed for JSON/YAML modes and template context
68	
69	Implementing the trait directly is useful when your handler needs internal state—database connections, configuration, caches, etc.
70	
71	### Example: Struct Handler with State
72	
73	```rust
74	use standout_dispatch::{Handler, Output, CommandContext, HandlerResult};
75	use clap::ArgMatches;
76	use serde::Serialize;
77	
78	struct CachingDatabase {
79	    connection: Connection,
80	    cache: HashMap<String, Vec<Row>>,
81	}
82	
83	impl CachingDatabase {
84	    fn query_with_cache(&mut self, sql: &str) -> Result<Vec<Row>, Error> {
85	        if let Some(cached) = self.cache.get(sql) {
86	            return Ok(cached.clone());
87	        }
88	        let result = self.connection.execute(sql)?;
89	        self.cache.insert(sql.to_string(), result.clone());
90	        Ok(result)
91	    }
92	}
93	
94	impl Handler for CachingDatabase {
95	    type Output = Vec<Row>;
96	
97	    fn handle(&mut self, matches: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<Vec<Row>> {
98	        let query: &String = matches.get_one("query").unwrap();
99	        let rows = self.query_with_cache(query)?;  // &mut self works!
100	        Ok(Output::Render(rows))
101	    }
102	}
103	```
104	
105	---
106	
107	## Closure Handlers
108	
109	Most handlers are simple closures using `FnHandler`:
110	
111	```rust
112	use standout_dispatch::{FnHandler, Output, HandlerResult};
113	
114	let mut counter = 0;
115	
116	let handler = FnHandler::new(move |_matches, _ctx| {
117	    counter += 1;  // Mutation works!
118	    Ok(Output::Render(counter))
119	});
120	```
121	
122	The closure signature:
123	
124	```rust
125	fn(&ArgMatches, &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<T>
126	where T: Serialize
127	```
128	
129	Closures are `FnMut`, allowing captured variables to be mutated.
130	
131	---
132	
133	## SimpleFnHandler (No Context Needed)
134	
135	When your handler doesn't need `CommandContext`, use `SimpleFnHandler` for a cleaner signature:
136	
137	```rust
138	use standout_dispatch::SimpleFnHandler;
139	
140	let handler = SimpleFnHandler::new(|matches| {
141	    let verbose = matches.get_flag("verbose");
142	    let items = storage::list()?;
143	    Ok(ListResult { items, verbose })
144	});
145	```
146	
147	The closure signature:
148	
149	```rust
150	fn(&ArgMatches) -> Result<T, E>
151	where T: Serialize, E: Into<anyhow::Error>
152	```
153	
154	`SimpleFnHandler` automatically wraps the result in `Output::Render` via `IntoHandlerResult`.
155	
156	---
157	
158	## IntoHandlerResult Trait
159	
160	The `IntoHandlerResult` trait enables handlers to return `Result<T, E>` directly instead of `HandlerResult<T>`:
161	
162	```rust
163	use standout_dispatch::IntoHandlerResult;
164	
165	// Before: explicit Output wrapping
166	fn list(_m: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<Vec<Item>> {
167	    let items = storage::list()?;
168	    Ok(Output::Render(items))
169	}
170	
171	// After: automatic conversion
172	fn list(_m: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> impl IntoHandlerResult<Vec<Item>> {
173	    storage::list()  // Result<Vec<Item>, Error> auto-converts
174	}
175	```
176	
177	The trait is implemented for:
178	
179	- `Result<T, E>` where `E: Into<anyhow::Error>` → wraps `Ok(t)` in `Output::Render(t)`
180	- `HandlerResult<T>` → passes through unchanged
181	
182	This is used internally by `SimpleFnHandler` and the `#[handler]` macro.
183	
184	---
185	
186	## HandlerResult
187	
188	`HandlerResult<T>` is a standard `Result` type:
189	
190	```rust
191	pub type HandlerResult<T> = Result<Output<T>, anyhow::Error>;
192	```
193	
194	The `?` operator works naturally for error propagation:
195	
196	```rust
197	fn list_handler(matches: &ArgMatches, ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<Items> {
198	    let items = storage::load()?;           // Propagates errors
199	    let filtered = filter_items(&items)?;   // Propagates errors
200	    Ok(Output::Render(Items { filtered }))
201	}
202	```
203	
204	### Authoritative external failures
205	
206	When a handler delegates to another executable and the application's contract
207	requires that executable's exact nonzero status and stderr, return the public
208	`ExternalFailure` type through the same `HandlerResult` seam:
209	
210	```rust
211	let failure = ExternalFailure::new(128, git_stderr)?;
212	Err(failure.into())
213	```
214	
215	Construction rejects status `0`. Standout recognizes only this concrete type,
216	preserves its diagnostic verbatim, and exposes it as `RunErrorKind::External`.
217	Ordinary handler errors still use status `1`; this is not a general exit-code
218	mapping mechanism. Handlers must not print or call `process::exit` themselves.
219	
220	---
221	
222	## The Output Enum
223	
224	`Output<T>` represents what a handler produces:
225	
226	```rust
227	#[non_exhaustive]
228	pub enum Output<T: Serialize> {
229	    Render(T),
230	    Silent,
231	    Binary { data: Vec<u8>, filename: String },
232	    Artifact(Artifact<T>),
233	}
234	```
235	
236	`Output` is `#[non_exhaustive]`: matches on it need a `_` arm so later shapes
237	can be added without breaking downstream code.
238	
239	### Output::Render(T)
240	
241	The common case. Data is passed to the render function:
242	
243	```rust
244	#[derive(Serialize)]
245	struct ListResult {
246	    items: Vec<Item>,
247	    total: usize,
248	}
249	
250	fn list_handler(_m: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<ListResult> {
251	    let items = storage::list()?;
252	    Ok(Output::Render(ListResult {
253	        total: items.len(),
254	        items,
255	    }))
256	}
257	```
258	
259	### Output::Silent
260	
261	No output produced. Useful for commands with side effects only:
262	
263	```rust
264	fn delete_handler(matches: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<()> {
265	    let id: &String = matches.get_one("id").unwrap();
266	    storage::delete(id)?;
267	    Ok(Output::Silent)
268	}
269	```
270	
271	Silent behavior:
272	
273	- Post-output hooks still receive `RenderedOutput::Silent`
274	- Render function is not called
275	- Nothing prints to stdout
276	
277	### Output::Binary
278	
279	Raw bytes for file output:
280	
281	```rust
282	fn export_handler(matches: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<()> {
283	    let data = generate_report()?;
284	    let pdf_bytes = render_to_pdf(&data)?;
285	
286	    Ok(Output::Binary {
287	        data: pdf_bytes,
288	        filename: "report.pdf".into(),
289	    })
290	}
291	```
292	
293	Binary output bypasses the render function entirely.
294	
295	The filename is a **hint for the caller**, not permission to write. Without
296	`--output-file-path`, `run()` sends the bytes to stdout and touches no file. If
297	you want the framework to write the suggested destination, use `Output::Artifact`
298	— that opt-in is the whole difference between the two shapes.
299	
300	### Output::Artifact
301	
302	Owned bytes plus an application-owned report, for commands that produce a file
303	*and* have something to say about it. `Output::Binary` cannot carry a report,
304	and nothing renders after its write, so a command that wants to say "exported 12
305	rows to /tmp/report.csv (2 warnings)" would otherwise have to write the file
306	itself — pulling destination policy back into the application core.
307	
308	```rust
309	use standout::cli::{Artifact, HandlerResult, Output};
310	
311	#[derive(Serialize)]
312	struct ExportReport {
313	    exported: usize,
314	    warnings: Vec<Warning>,
315	}
316	
317	fn export_handler(_m: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<ExportReport> {
318	    let export = core::export_csv()?;   // bytes + facts, no filesystem
319	
320	    Ok(Output::Artifact(
321	        Artifact::new(export.csv)
322	            .suggest_destination(export.suggested_filename)
323	            .with_report(ExportReport {
324	                exported: export.rows,
325	                warnings: export.warnings,
326	            }),
327	    ))
328	}
329	```
330	
331	Who owns what:
332	
333	| Concern | Owner |
334	| --- | --- |
335	| Artifact bytes | Application |
336	| Suggested destination | Application (a suggestion) |
337	| Semantic report and warning taxonomy | Application |
338	| Destination selection | Framework |
339	| The write and its failure | Framework |
340	| Receipt (completed destination) | Framework |
341	
342	#### Destination policy
343	
344	Standout selects the destination deterministically:
345	
346	1. the explicit `--output-file-path` override;
347	2. the artifact's `suggest_destination(...)`, if the application opted in;
348	3. stdout, if the application opted in with `allow_stdout()`.
349	
350	If none applies, the run fails with `FinalWrite(Artifact)` rather than inventing
351	a file or dropping the bytes. All three steps share that one failure path.
352	
353	#### Write first, report second
354	
355	Standout writes, then renders the report from a fixed envelope:
356	
357	```json
358	{
359	  "report": { "exported": 12, "warnings": [] },
360	  "receipt": { "destination": "/tmp/report.csv", "stdout": false, "byte_count": 480 }
361	}
362	```
363	
364	So a template can say what only the framework knows:
365	
366	```jinja
367	Exported {{ report.exported }} rows to {{ receipt.destination }}
368	```
369	
370	The envelope shape is fixed (`report` + `receipt`) whatever the report's type,
371	so no application key can collide with the receipt. Structured modes serialize
372	the same envelope. A failed write renders nothing: success cannot outrun the
373	write that justifies it.
374	
375	#### The report channel
376	
377	Mixing a report into the bytes would corrupt them, so the channel follows the
378	destination:
379	
380	| Artifact destination | Report goes to |
381	| --- | --- |
382	| File | stdout |
383	| Stdout (`allow_stdout()`) | stderr |
384	
385	#### Hooks and artifacts
386	
387	Post-dispatch hooks see the report as ordinary handler data. Post-output hooks
388	see `RenderedOutput::Artifact` and can still transform the bytes or the report
389	via `as_artifact_mut()`. Hooks never perform the write — that stays framework-
390	owned, which is what keeps the failure path single and the report honest.
391	
392	Bytes are owned; streaming is deliberately not part of this contract.
393	
394	---
395	
396	## CommandContext
397	
398	`CommandContext` provides execution environment information and state access:
399	
400	```rust
401	pub struct CommandContext {
402	    pub command_path: Vec<String>,
403	    pub app_state: Rc<Extensions>,
404	    pub extensions: Extensions,
405	}
406	```
407	
408	**command_path**: The subcommand chain as a vector, e.g., `["db", "migrate"]`. Useful for logging or conditional logic.
409	
410	**app_state**: Shared, immutable state configured at app build time via `AppBuilder::app_state()`. Wrapped in `Arc` for cheap cloning. Use for database connections, configuration, API clients.
411	
412	**extensions**: Per-request, mutable state injected by pre-dispatch hooks. Use for user sessions, request IDs, computed values.
413	
414	> For comprehensive coverage of state management, see [App State and Extensions](app-state.md).
415	
416	---
417	
418	## State Access: App State vs Extensions
419	
420	Handlers access state through two distinct mechanisms with different semantics:
421	
422	| Aspect         | `ctx.app_state`               | `ctx.extensions`           |
423	| -------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------- |
424	| **Mutability** | Immutable (`&`)               | Mutable (`&mut`)           |
425	| **Lifetime**   | App lifetime                  | Per-request                |
426	| **Set by**     | `AppBuilder::app_state()`     | Pre-dispatch hooks         |
427	| **Use for**    | Database, Config, API clients | User sessions, request IDs |
428	
429	### App State (Shared Resources)
430	
431	Configure long-lived resources at build time:
432	
433	```rust
434	App::builder()
435	    .app_state(Database::connect()?)
436	    .app_state(Config::load()?)
437	    .command("list", list_handler, template)?
438	    .build()?
439	```
440	
441	Access in handlers via `ctx.app_state`:
442	
443	```rust
444	fn list_handler(matches: &ArgMatches, ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<Vec<Item>> {
445	    let db = ctx.app_state.get_required::<Database>()?;
446	    let config = ctx.app_state.get_required::<Config>()?;
447	
448	    let items = db.query_items(config.max_results)?;
449	    Ok(Output::Render(items))
450	}
451	```
452	
453	### Extensions (Per-Request State)
454	
455	Pre-dispatch hooks inject request-scoped state:
456	
457	```rust
458	use standout_dispatch::{Hooks, HookError};
459	
460	struct UserScope { user_id: String, permissions: Vec<String> }
461	
462	let hooks = Hooks::new()
463	    .pre_dispatch(|matches, ctx| {
464	        // Can read app_state to set up per-request state
465	        let db = ctx.app_state.get_required::<Database>()?;
466	
467	        let user_id = matches.get_one::<String>("user").unwrap().clone();
468	        let permissions = db.get_permissions(&user_id)?;
469	
470	        ctx.extensions.insert(UserScope { user_id, permissions });
471	        Ok(())
472	    });
473	```
474	
475	Handlers retrieve from extensions:
476	
477	```rust
478	fn list_handler(matches: &ArgMatches, ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<Vec<Item>> {
479	    let db = ctx.app_state.get_required::<Database>()?;       // shared
480	    let scope = ctx.extensions.get_required::<UserScope>()?;  // per-request
481	
482	    let items = db.list_for_user(&scope.user_id)?;
483	    Ok(Output::Render(items))
484	}
485	```
486	
487	### Extensions API
488	
489	Both `app_state` and `extensions` use the same `Extensions` type with these methods:
490	
491	| Method              | Description                                     |
492	| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
493	| `insert<T>(value)`  | Insert a value, returns previous if any         |
494	| `get<T>()`          | Get immutable reference, returns `Option<&T>`   |
495	| `get_required<T>()` | Get reference or return error if missing        |
496	| `get_mut<T>()`      | Get mutable reference, returns `Option<&mut T>` |
497	| `remove<T>()`       | Remove and return value                         |
498	| `contains<T>()`     | Check if type exists                            |
499	| `len()`             | Number of stored values                         |
500	| `is_empty()`        | True if no values stored                        |
501	| `clear()`           | Remove all values                               |
502	
503	Use `get_required` for mandatory dependencies (fails fast with clear error), `get` for optional ones.
504	
505	### When to Use Which
506	
507	**Use App State for:**
508	
509	- Database connections — expensive to create, should be pooled
510	- Configuration — loaded once at startup
511	- API clients — shared HTTP clients with connection pooling
512	
513	**Use Extensions for:**
514	
515	- User context — current user, session, permissions
516	- Request metadata — request ID, timing, correlation ID
517	- Transient state — data computed by one hook, used by handler
518	
519	### The Two-State Pattern
520	
521	The separation exists because:
522	
523	1. **Closure capture doesn't work with `#[derive(Dispatch)]`** — macro-generated dispatch calls handlers with a fixed signature
524	2. **App-level resources shouldn't be created per-request** — database pools and config are expensive
525	3. **Per-request state needs mutable injection** — hooks compute values at runtime
526	
527	```rust
528	// App state: configured once at build time
529	App::builder()
530	    .app_state(Database::connect()?)  // Shared via Arc
531	    .hooks("users.list", Hooks::new()
532	        .pre_dispatch(|matches, ctx| {
533	            // Extensions: computed per-request, can use app_state
534	            let db = ctx.app_state.get_required::<Database>()?;
535	            let user = authenticate(matches, db)?;
536	            ctx.extensions.insert(user);
537	            Ok(())
538	        }))?
539	```
540	
541	> For comprehensive coverage of state management patterns, see [App State and Extensions](app-state.md).
542	
543	---
544	
545	## Accessing CLI Arguments
546	
547	The `ArgMatches` parameter provides access to parsed arguments through clap's standard API:
548	
549	```rust
550	fn handler(matches: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<Data> {
551	    // Flags
552	    let verbose = matches.get_flag("verbose");
553	
554	    // Required options
555	    let name: &String = matches.get_one("name").unwrap();
556	
557	    // Optional values
558	    let limit: Option<&u32> = matches.get_one("limit");
559	
560	    // Multiple values
561	    let tags: Vec<&String> = matches.get_many("tags")
562	        .map(|v| v.collect())
563	        .unwrap_or_default();
564	
565	    Ok(Output::Render(Data { ... }))
566	}
567	```
568	
569	For subcommands, you work with the `ArgMatches` for your specific command level.
570	
571	---
572	
573	## Testing Handlers
574	
575	Because handlers have explicit inputs and outputs, their adapter behavior is
576	straightforward to test directly. Test validation, filtering, and state
577	transitions through the CLI-free library instead:
578	
579	```rust
580	#[test]
581	fn test_list_handler() {
582	    let cmd = Command::new("test")
583	        .arg(Arg::new("verbose").long("verbose").action(ArgAction::SetTrue));
584	    let matches = cmd.try_get_matches_from(["test", "--verbose"]).unwrap();
585	
586	    let ctx = CommandContext {
587	        command_path: vec!["list".into()],
588	        ..Default::default()
589	    };
590	
591	    let result = list_handler(&matches, &ctx);
592	
593	    assert!(result.is_ok());
594	    if let Ok(Output::Render(data)) = result {
595	        assert!(data.verbose);
596	    }
597	}
598	```
599	
600	No mocking frameworks needed—construct `ArgMatches` with clap, create a `CommandContext`, call your handler, assert on the result.
601	
602	### Testing with App State
603	
604	When handlers depend on app_state, inject test fixtures:
605	
606	```rust
607	#[test]
608	fn test_handler_with_app_state() {
609	    use std::sync::Arc;
610	
611	    // Create test fixtures
612	    let mock_db = MockDatabase::with_items(vec![
613	        Item { id: "1", name: "Test" }
614	    ]);
615	
616	    // Build app_state with test data
617	    let mut app_state = Extensions::new();
618	    app_state.insert(mock_db);
619	
620	    let ctx = CommandContext {
621	        command_path: vec!["list".into()],
622	        app_state: Arc::new(app_state),
623	        extensions: Extensions::new(),
624	    };
625	
626	    let cmd = Command::new("test");
627	    let matches = cmd.try_get_matches_from(["test"]).unwrap();
628	
629	    let result = list_handler(&matches, &ctx);
630	    assert!(result.is_ok());
631	}
632	```

634	### Testing Handlers with Mutable State
635	
636	Handler tests can verify state mutation across calls:
637	
638	```rust
639	#[test]
640	fn test_handler_state_mutation() {
641	    struct Counter { count: u32 }
642	
643	    impl Handler for Counter {
644	        type Output = u32;
645	        fn handle(&mut self, _m: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<u32> {
646	            self.count += 1;
647	            Ok(Output::Render(self.count))
648	        }
649	    }
650	
651	    let mut handler = Counter { count: 0 };
652	    let cmd = Command::new("test");
653	    let matches = cmd.try_get_matches_from(["test"]).unwrap();
654	    let ctx = CommandContext {
655	        command_path: vec!["count".into()],
656	        ..Default::default()
657	    };
658	
659	    // State accumulates across calls
660	    let _ = handler.handle(&matches, &ctx);
661	    let _ = handler.handle(&matches, &ctx);
662	    let result = handler.handle(&matches, &ctx);
663	
664	    assert!(matches!(result, Ok(Output::Render(3))));
665	}
